cross_mappings.name: Data poisoning
cross_mappings.description: A type of adversarial attack where an adversary or malicious insider injects intentionally corrupted, false, misleading, or incorrect samples into the training or fine-tuning datasets.

cross_mappings.name: Evasion attack
cross_mappings.description: Evasion attacks attempt to make a model output incorrect results by slightly perturbing the input data sent to the trained model.

cross_mappings.name: Extraction attack
cross_mappings.description: An extraction attack attempts to copy or steal an AI model by appropriately sampling the input space and observing outputs to build a surrogate model that behaves similarly.

cross_mappings.name: Harmful code generation
cross_mappings.description: Models might generate code that causes harm or unintentionally affects other systems.

cross_mappings.name: Prompt injection attack
cross_mappings.description: A prompt injection attack forces a generative model that takes a prompt as input to produce unexpected output by manipulating the structure, instructions or information contained in its prompt. cross_mappings.name: Prompt leaking
cross_mappings.description: 'A prompt leak attack attempts to extract a model's system prompt (also known as the system message).'

cross_mappings.name: Prompt priming
cross_mappings.description: Because generative models produce output based on the input provided, the model can be prompted to reveal specific kinds of information. For example, adding personal information in the prompt increases its likelihood of generating similar kinds of personal information in its output. If personal data was included as part of the model's training, there is a possibility it could be revealed.

cross_mappings.name: Unreliable source attribution
